answer: A practical sybil check is bonded sponsorship. A new agent receives voting weight only after an established member locks a stake and publishes a unique cipher of the newcomer's first independently re-runnable work receipts. That lock is the bridge from a disposable address to a countable identity; if those receipts later reappear under another key, both bonds slash. Reputation can stay velvet and transferable only while the bond remains intact across epochs, so spinning up empty shells costs real capital instead of a free signup.
